_comment: Stage D = per-seed universe generation (S1) + process noise (S2). The first STOCHASTIC rung and the first where a policy cannot succeed by exploiting one particular world. Observation vector unchanged - what changes is which components matter (plan.md 5).

noise._comment: S2 only. process_sigma is a per-step velocity impulse - over 500 steps that is a random walk of about sqrt(500)*0.002 = 0.045, set against v_capture 0.6, so it is felt at the capture gate without swamping it. thrust_jitter 0.03 is the misfire from plan.md 2.6. S3 observation noise stays OFF until Stage F.

_obs_note: None. The vector is unchanged from Stage C - control_authority and fuel_fraction have been present and unnecessary since Stage A, and the PREDICTION for this rung is that robustness promotes them. That is the whole point of freezing the superset.

dispatch._comment: 8 distinct WORLDS per generation, each flown 4 times to fill a 32-episode batch. The repeat is what gives Trainer.update a real per-world baseline; without it every episode is a different universe seen once and the advantage mostly encodes which draw was easy. Eight distinct worlds still means eight visibly different sandboxes.

training._tuning_note: lr 1e-3 carried from Stage C, where 4e-3 was MEASURED to diverge on a warm start. Warm-started from the Stage C champion (held-out 0.83 phase / 0.96 layout), which is the first Stage C champion strong enough to be worth transferring - the pre-brake one scored 0.00 and would have transferred nothing.
training._curriculum_note: MEASURED: warm-starting the Stage C champion straight into full randomisation sits at 0.04-0.08 held-out for 120 generations with NO trend - closest approach stays at ~1.6, so the craft never even enters the braking basin (sigma ~1.05). The blocker is orientation: Stages A-C always ran the same craft->portal corridor, and several observation components (craft_vel, a_grav) are in the ABSOLUTE frame, so a rotated world is unrecognisable to that policy. The ramp therefore widens orientation alongside N and eccentricity - difficulty 0 is deliberately Stage-C-like - and reaches the full distribution by generation 90, leaving 60 generations on the real one. Held-out evaluation is ALWAYS pinned at difficulty 1.0.
training._lr_note: 3e-4 is the best of a measured sweep (3e-4 -> 0.125, 1e-4 -> 0.042, 3e-5 -> 0.042 best held-out over 60 generations). Lower rates do NOT preserve the warm start: they freeze the policy at its transferred state, which is already poor at difficulty 1.0 (the Stage C champion scores 0.62 at difficulty 0 but 0.06 at difficulty 1.0). The large gradient norms seen at 1e-3 (3.6-4.0 against a 1.0 clip) are a symptom of the value head mispredicting on unseen worlds, not the root cause.
